title: Saul spares Agag — 1 Samuel 15
paragraphs: He just spared one king God said to destroy.

In 1 Samuel 15, Saul won the battle but lost the word of the Lord. God gave a clear command. No loopholes. No edits. No partial obedience. But Saul kept Agag alive and saved the best sheep and cattle, then dressed it up like worship. He called compromise “sacrifice.” He called rebellion “obedience.”
And that’s still how sin talks.

We do not always deny God with open wickedness. Sometimes we do it with selective surrender. We cut down most of the Amalekites in our lives—but spare the Agag we secretly admire. The appetite. The pride. The relationship. The habit. The wound we keep feeding. The thing God said kill, and we renamed “not that serious.”

Partial obedience is still disobedience.
And delayed surrender is still rebellion.

Samuel’s words still thunder: “To obey is better than sacrifice.” Saul wanted the appearance of devotion without the cost of full submission. And many still do. Church attendance. Worship hands lifted. Bible verses posted. But one Agag hidden in the shadows.
The Lord is not asking for your polished excuse. He is asking for your surrender.
And that is where grace walks in.

Because where Saul lost a kingdom through disobedience, Jesus secured an eternal Kingdom through perfect obedience. Saul spared what God told him to destroy. Jesus destroyed what was destroying us—sin, guilt, death, condemnation—by His cross. He did not negotiate with evil. He crushed it. And now in Christ, the power to obey does not come from human willpower, but from a new heart made alive by grace.
So do not protect what God is calling you to put to death.
Bring your Agag into the light.
There is mercy for the compromised. There is cleansing for the double-minded. There is restoration for the one who has been playing holy while sparing sin. Jesus still receives the repentant.

Kill what God condemned.
And cling to the Christ who obeyed in your place.
